title: 1984 AHSME Problem 28
statement: The number of distinct pairs of integers \((x,y)\) such that \[ \begin{aligned} 0&\lt x\lt y,\\ \sqrt{1984}&=\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{y} \end{aligned} \] is

solutions.text:
Because \(\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{y}=8\sqrt{31},\) the two radicals must have common squarefree part \(31.\) Write \(x=31u^2\) and \(y=31v^2\) for positive integers \(u,v.\) Then \[ u+v=8,\qquad u\lt v. \] The possibilities are \((u,v)=(1,7),\) \((2,6),\) and \((3,5),\) producing three distinct pairs \((x,y).\)

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: Use \(1984=31\cdot8^2\) and write both radicands with a common squarefree part
Set \(x=31u^2,\ y=31v^2\) and count positive integers \(u\lt v\) with \(u+v=8\)
